# Chapter 47: Production Deployment & MLOps at Scale

> "Software is eating the world. In healthcare, reliable software
> deployments can be the difference between a patient getting the
> right care and not getting it at all."
>
> — adapted from Marc Andreessen (2011)

## 47.1 The Production Gap

Academic models rarely reach clinicians.  The gap between a working Jupyter
notebook and a reliable production system involves:

- **Reproducibility**: Exact dependency pinning, deterministic builds
- **Reliability**: Health checks, graceful degradation, rolling updates
- **Observability**: Logging, metrics, distributed tracing
- **Drift detection**: Model performance monitored in production (Vol 6 MLOps)
- **Regulatory compliance**: HIPAA audit trails, data lineage, access controls

This chapter closes the loop from the algorithms in Vols 3–6 to a
production-ready healthcare API.

## 47.2 Package Registry Submission

All 11 textbook packages can be registered in a custom Julia registry,
enabling `Pkg.add("CausalHealth")` for users.

### 47.2.1 Registry Structure

```
OpenHealthcareGIS-registry/
├── Registry.toml
├── CausalHealth/
│   ├── Package.toml
│   ├── Versions.toml
│   ├── Compat.toml
│   └── Deps.toml
└── GaussianProcessHealth/
    └── ...
```

### 47.2.2 Automation

```julia
include("scripts/registry_submission.jl")

# Generate all registry entries
main(;
    output_dir = "OpenHealthcareGIS-registry",
    repo_root  = ".",
    dry_run    = false,
)
# Generates: Registry.toml + Package/Versions/Compat/Deps.toml for each package
# Also generates: pr_body.md for JuliaRegistries/General PR

# Preview PR body
println(generate_pr_body())
```

### 47.2.3 Installing from the Custom Registry

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.Registry.add(RegistrySpec(
    url = "https://github.com/timothyhartzog/OpenHealthcareGIS-registry"
))
Pkg.add(["CausalHealth", "GaussianProcessHealth", "DeepHealth", "BayesianHealth"])
```

## 47.3 Kubernetes Deployment

### 47.3.1 Architecture

```
Internet → NGINX Ingress (TLS) → Service (ClusterIP)
                                      ↓
                               Deployment (3 pods)
                               ├── Pod 1: healthcare-gis-api
                               ├── Pod 2: healthcare-gis-api
                               └── Pod 3: healthcare-gis-api
                                      ↓
                               PVC (model storage, 10Gi)
                                      ↓
                               PostgreSQL + PostGIS service
```

### 47.3.2 Generating Manifests

```julia
include("scripts/k8s_deployment.jl")

cfg = K8sConfig(;
    namespace      = "healthcare-gis-prod",
    app_name       = "healthcare-gis-api",
    image          = "ghcr.io/timothyhartzog/geo-julia",
    image_tag      = "v0.7.0",
    replicas       = 3,
    cpu_request    = "500m",
    cpu_limit      = "2000m",
    memory_limit   = "2Gi",
    julia_threads  = 4,
    ingress_host   = "api.healthcaregis.nd.gov",
    min_replicas   = 2,
    max_replicas   = 10,
)

paths = generate_k8s_manifests(cfg; output_dir="k8s/prod")
# ✓ 00-namespace.yaml (8 lines)
# ✓ 01-configmap.yaml (20 lines)
# ✓ 03-deployment.yaml (85 lines)
# ✓ 05-hpa.yaml (40 lines)
# ...

# Deploy
# kubectl apply -f k8s/prod/
```

### 47.3.3 Key Production Patterns

**Rolling updates** (zero-downtime deployment):
```yaml
strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 1
    maxUnavailable: 0
```

**Startup probe** (allow up to 5 minutes for Julia JIT compilation):
```yaml
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /api/v2/health
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 30   # 10s × 30 = 5 minutes
```

**Horizontal Pod Autoscaler** scales 2–10 replicas based on CPU:

$$\text{desired\_replicas} = \lceil \text{current\_replicas} \times \frac{\text{current\_CPU}}{\text{target\_CPU}} \rceil$$

## 47.4 CI/CD Pipeline

### 47.4.1 GitHub Actions Workflow

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml (excerpt)
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: julia-actions/setup-julia@v2
        with: { version: "1.10" }
      - run: julia --project=. -e 'import Pkg; Pkg.test()'

  build:
    needs: test
    steps:
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/timothyhartzog/geo-julia:${{ github.ref_name }}

  deploy:
    needs: build
    environment: production
    steps:
      - run: |
          kubectl -n healthcare-gis set image \
            deployment/healthcare-gis-api \
            healthcare-gis-api=ghcr.io/timothyhartzog/geo-julia:${{ github.ref_name }}
          kubectl -n healthcare-gis rollout status deployment/healthcare-gis-api
```

```julia
# Generate the full CD workflow
cfg = K8sConfig()
generate_github_workflow_cd(cfg; output_path=".github/workflows/deploy.yml")
```

## 47.5 Benchmarking

Before deploying, benchmark all algorithms on production-representative data:

```julia
include("scripts/benchmark_suite.jl")

results = run_benchmark_suite(; quick=false)
# Prints cross-volume timing table:
# ┌─ Linear Algebra
# │  Cholesky (GP)                    100×100      0.04 ms      0.06 ms  —
# │  SVD                              100×100      0.29 ms      0.35 ms  —
# ┌─ Gaussian Processes
# │  Exact GP                         n=50         0.8 ms       1.1 ms   —
# │  Exact GP                         n=100        5.2 ms       6.8 ms   —
# ┌─ Deep Learning
# │  MLP forward (h=32)               100×8×32     0.02 ms      0.03 ms  —
```

### Performance Targets

| API endpoint | Latency p95 | Throughput |
|-------------|-------------|-----------|
| `/api/v2/health` | < 5 ms | > 1000 RPS |
| `/api/v2/catchment/50` | < 100 ms | > 50 RPS |
| `/api/v2/state` | < 500 ms | > 10 RPS |
| `/api/v2/events` (SSE) | streaming | N/A |

## 47.6 Production Monitoring

Combine the MLOps drift detection from Vol 6 with the deployment:

```julia
# Scheduled job: every 30 minutes
include("vol6_advanced_inference/scripts/mlops_pipeline.jl")

function production_health_check(registry, X_reference, X_recent)
    # 1. Drift detection
    drift = detect_drift(X_reference, X_recent; feature_names=feature_names)
    n_drifted = sum(d.drifted for d in drift)
    println("Features drifted: $n_drifted / $(length(drift))")

    # 2. Performance check
    trigger = RetrainingTrigger(0.15, 0.1, 100)
    result = should_retrain(trigger, drift, current_rmse, baseline_rmse, n_new_samples)

    if result.should_retrain
        println("ALERT: Retraining triggered — $(result.reason)")
        # Trigger retraining pipeline via CI/CD
    end
end
```

## 47.7 Summary: From Algorithm to Production

The complete journey of a healthcare access model:

```
Vol 3: Spatial data → E2SFCA access scores (geographic features)
Vol 4: Spatial stats → Hot-spot detection, autocorrelation
Vol 5: ML models → RF/GBM predictions, feature engineering
Vol 6: Causal inference → Policy effect estimation (DiD, IV)
Vol 6: GP regression → Uncertainty-quantified access surfaces
Vol 6: MLOps → Drift detection, A/B testing, model registry
Vol 7: Deep learning → MLP/GNN/TabNet for complex patterns
Vol 7: Bayesian → Full posterior inference, model comparison
Vol 7: Production → K8s deployment, CI/CD, benchmarking
```

Every algorithm in this textbook is:
- **Implemented** in pure Julia (no opaque black boxes)
- **Tested** with 15–20 unit tests per package
- **Documented** with Documenter.jl API references
- **Benchmarked** against each other
- **Deployable** via the K8s manifests and CI/CD workflows in this chapter
